title: D-FINE-L vs RT-DETR-R50: benchmark on the same protocol
dek: Measured on the same COCO protocol: D-FINE-L leads by 4.1 mAP points with fewer parameters, but RT-DETR-R50 is 26.58% faster on desktop GPU.
author: Vision Analysis

blocks.text: D-FINE-L is the more accurate model: 60.0 vs 55.9 mAP@50-95 against RT-DETR-R50 on an RTX 5070 Ti in PyTorch, and it reaches that with fewer parameters (31.24M vs 42.89M) and less VRAM (245 vs 326 MB). RT-DETR-R50 is the faster detector on that GPU: 29.8 vs 21.9 FPS, a 26.58% edge. The speed order flips on Jetson Orin and Raspberry Pi 5, where D-FINE-L pulls ahead. Pick by deployment target.

D-FINE-L (31.24M parameters, Apache-2.0) and RT-DETR-R50 (42.89M, Apache-2.0) both evaluate at 640 px input, so the input resolution matches and does not skew the comparison. D-FINE-L is the smaller model here. Both have verified rows on desktop GPU, A100, Jetson Orin, and Raspberry Pi 5, so this comparison covers the deploy targets where the answer changes.

blocks.caption: Accuracy vs parameters on COCO val2017. D-FINE-L and RT-DETR-R50 highlighted against the full set.

blocks.text: mAP is shown in percent form. D-FINE-L measures 60.0 mAP@50-95 to RT-DETR-R50's 55.9, a 4.1 point lead. The gap is wider on small objects: 45.9 vs 38.3 mAP_small, a 20.07% relative difference. D-FINE-L reaches that accuracy with fewer parameters than RT-DETR-R50.
On the RTX 5070 Ti, RT-DETR-R50 runs 29.8 FPS to D-FINE-L's 21.9 in PyTorch, a 26.58% edge. The gap holds under conversion: 62.8 vs 50.9 FPS on ONNX Runtime, 87.4 vs 72.3 FPS on TensorRT FP32.

The speed verdict does not travel to the edge. On Jetson Orin, D-FINE-L runs 4.7 FPS to RT-DETR-R50's 4.3; on Raspberry Pi 5, 0.4 to 0.3. If your target is an edge board, the desktop numbers point the wrong way.

Pick D-FINE-L when accuracy or memory matters, or when you deploy to Jetson Orin or a Raspberry Pi: it is more accurate at every object size, uses less VRAM, and is the faster model on both edge boards. Pick RT-DETR-R50 for desktop or server GPU throughput, where it leads on every GPU runtime measured. Both ship under Apache-2.0, so licensing does not force the choice.

# pip install libreyolo
from libreyolo import LibreYOLO

dfine = LibreYOLO("LibreDFINEl.pt")     # 31.24M params, 60.0 mAP@50-95
rtdetr = LibreYOLO("LibreRTDETRr50.pt") # 42.89M params, 55.9 mAP@50-95

results = dfine("image.jpg")
